mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer savings (proxied by RSAFS) signals both tighter monetary policy and reduced household liquidity, amplifying the discount rate effect and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls month-over-month
regime_hint: high policy rate with falling household savings
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate and payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market churning with net job destruction, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index above 4% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts anticipatory monetary tightening and erodes real corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of current regime.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY change > 4% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.
